claims.text: Integrating CALPHAD modeling with targeted DSC measurements enables accurate and efficient determination of fusion and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across high-entropy alloys.
The relevant initial materials are solid, compositionally complex, near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD can predict melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, melting volume change, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Targeted DSC measurements can calibrate and validate CALPHAD predictions for HEAs.
Reliable assessed binary and ternary subsystem data are important for applying CALPHAD successfully to HEAs.
Configurational entropy contributes to phase stability in compositionally complex alloys.
CALPHAD represents phase stability through enthalpic and entropic contributions to Gibbs energy.
CALPHAD quantitatively captures configurational contributions relevant to fusion properties in HEAs.
DSC can precisely measure heat-capacity jumps and latent heat at melting for HEAs.
DSC can precisely measure volume changes at melting.
Experimental calibration can compensate for database limitations and make calculated phase equilibria and transformation properties match observations.
The integrated method will predict fusion properties within approximately 5–10% of high-resolution DSC values.
The integrated method improves on traditional single-method approaches.
Traditional experimental determination of HEA thermodynamic properties commonly requires extensive trial-and-error and empirical fitting.
Standalone CALPHAD predictions for HEAs are uncertain when multicomponent thermodynamic data are limited.
The approach should be robust for HEAs with sufficient assessed binary and ternary subsystem data.
The approach may be less reliable where thermodynamic database information is sparse.
Even with adequate binary and ternary data, transformation temperatures, phase compositions, and phase fractions can remain difficult to predict by CALPHAD.
Dilatometry can independently measure volume changes at the melting transition.

contradictions.description: The mechanism assigns measurement of melting volume change to DSC, whereas the validation design assigns that measurement to complementary dilatometry.

The claimed performance target is 5–10% error, but the approach is rejected only if over half of compositions exceed 15% error. It could therefore fail its stated accuracy target without satisfying the proposed falsification rule.
